## Natural history notes

A small grass skipper characterized by warm orange-brown wings, darker wing borders, and a tawny-orange edge along the forewing that gives the species its name. In Florida, it is found in open grassy habitats such as prairies, fields, roadsides, pastures, marsh edges, lawns, and other sunny areas where grasses are abundant. Adults feed on nectar from low flowers, while the caterpillars feed on grasses, using folded or tied grass blades as shelters during development.
